ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يس (١) وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ (٢)).
The majority read the nūn with a sukūn, and its counterpart has been mentioned [Translator's note: i.e. earlier in the book]. Some of them pronounce the nūn distinctly (iẓhār), because by that he makes its sukūn real, whereas in the nasalisation (ghunna) there is something that brings it close to a vowel for the sake of pure continuous reading; and in the iẓhār there is a bringing of the letter close to pausing on it.
Some of them give the nūn a kasra, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two sukūns, and some of them give it a fatḥa, just as the fatḥa is given in أَيْنَ; and it has been said: the fatḥa is a case-ending (iʿrāb). And (يس) is a name of the sura, like هَابِيل [Translator's note: i.e. a non-Arabic proper name, and so a diptote], and the implied form is: "Recite Yā Sīn" (اتْلُ يس). (وَالْقِرَانِ) [Translator's note: so spelled in the source]: an oath on every view.

ukberi-tibyan:3-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ (٣) عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٤) تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ (٥) لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا مَا أُنْذِرَ آبَاؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَافِلُونَ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى صِرَاطٍ): it is a second khabar (predicate) of إنّ [Translator's note: the source prints لَإِنْ], and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase.
(تَنْزِيلَ الْعَزِيزِ), i.e. "it is the sending down of the Mighty" (هُوَ تَنْزِيلُ الْعَزِيزِ); the maṣdar (verbal noun) has the meaning of the passive participle, i.e. "that which is sent down by the Mighty" (مُنَزَّلُ الْعَزِيزِ). It is read in the accusative, as a maṣdar, i.e. "with a sending down" (تَنْزِيلًا); and also in the genitive, as an adjective of «الْقُرْآن».
(لِتُنْذِرَ): the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَنْزِيل, or attached to the meaning of His saying «مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ», i.e. "sent so that you may warn" (مُرْسَلٌ لِتُنْذِرَ).
And (مَا) is negating. It has been said: it has the meaning of الَّذِي (the relative "which"), i.e. "you warn them of the punishment of which their forefathers were warned" (تُنْذِرُهُمُ الْعَذَابَ الَّذِي أَنْذَرَهُ آبَاؤُهُمْ).
It has been said: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa). And it has been said: it is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَغْشَيْنَاهُمْ): with ghayn, i.e. "We covered the eyes of their insight"; so the muḍāf (first term of the construct) is omitted.
It is also read with ʿayn [Translator's note: i.e. فَأَعْشَيْنَاهُمْ], i.e. "We weakened their insight from perceiving guidance", just as the eye of one with night-blindness (الْأَعْشَى) is weak.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا وَآثَارَهُمْ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فِي إِمَامٍ مُبِينٍ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ): like (وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ) [al-Isrāʾ: 13], and it has already been dealt with.

ukberi-tibyan:13-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ (١٣) إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمُ اثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ فَقَالُوا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُمْ مُرْسَلُونَ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ): «اضْرِبْ» here has the meaning of "make" (اجْعَلْ); «أَصْحَابَ» is the first mafʿūl (object), and «مَثَلًا» is the second mafʿūl.
It has been said: it has the meaning of "mention" (اذْكُرْ), and the implied form is: "a likeness, the likeness of the people" (مَثَلًا مِثْلَ أَصْحَابِ); so the second is a badal (substitute) from the first.
And (إِذْ جَاءَهَا) is like «إِذِ انْتَبَذَتْ», and it has already been dealt with.
And the second (إِذْ) is a badal (substitute) from the first.
(فَعَزَزْنَا) is read with a doubled consonant and with a single one, and the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, i.e. "We strengthened the two of them" (قَوَّيْنَاهُمَا).

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكُمْ أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُسْرِفُونَ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ): in the form of a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "if you are reminded, you disbelieve" (إِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ كَفَرْتُمْ), or the like.
It is also read with a fatḥa on the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. أَأَنْ], i.e. "because you were reminded" (لِأَنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ). And it is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading: «أَيْنَ ذُكِرْتُمْ», i.e. "your evil deed clings to you wherever you are mentioned"; and the kāf is without doubling on this view.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا لِيَ لَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا لِيَ): the majority read the yāʾ with a fatḥa, because what follows it is treated as joined to it, since it is not good to pause on it and begin with what follows it. And (مَالِي لَا أَرَى الْهُدْهُدَ) is the reverse of that.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَأَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً إِنْ يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمَنُ بِضُرٍّ لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُنْقِذُونِ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تُغْنِ عَنِّي): it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and «مَا» may not stand in place of «لَا» here, because «مَا» negates what is in the present, whereas the apodosis of a condition is future and nothing else.

ukberi-tibyan:26-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يَا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ (٢٦) بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي): there are three views on «مَا». The first: it is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), i.e. "of His forgiving" (بِغُفْرَانِهِ). The second: it has the meaning of الَّذِي, i.e. "of the sin which He forgave" (بِالذَّنْبِ الَّذِي غَفَرَهُ). The third: it is an interrogative expressing magnification; some people mentioned it, and it is far-fetched, because when a preposition comes before the interrogative «مَا», its alif is dropped; though it has occurred in poetry without the dropping.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِنْ جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنْزِلِينَ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا): «مَا» is negating, and likewise in «وَمَا كُنَّا».
It is also permissible that the second «مَا» be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "and indeed We were" (وَقَدْ كُنَّا).
And it has been said: it is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «جُنْدٍ».

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً): the noun (ism) of كَانَ is implied (muḍmar), i.e. "the cry was nothing but a cry" (مَا كَانَتِ الصَّيْحَةُ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً); the purpose is to describe it as single. And إِذَا is for surprise (mufājaʾa). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:30-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (٣٠) أَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَاحَسْرَةً): there are two views on it. The first: «حَسْرَةً» is the one addressed (munādā), i.e. "O regret, come! For this is your time."
And (عَلَى) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَسْرَة; that is why it was put in the accusative, as in your saying: "O you who are striking a man" (يَا ضَارِبًا رَجُلًا). The second: the one addressed is omitted, and «حَسْرَةً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "I lament with a lament" (أَتَحَسَّرُ حَسْرَةً).
It is read among the irregular (shādhdh) readings «يَا حَسْرَةَ الْعِبَادِ», i.e. "O their lamenting!" (يَا تَحْسِيرَهُمْ); so the maṣdar is annexed to its agent. It may also be annexed to its object, i.e. "I lament over the servants" (أَتَحَسَّرُ عَلَى الْعِبَادِ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ): the clause is an explanation of the cause of the regret.
(وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا): it has already been dealt with.
(وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ): with a fatḥa on the hamza; it is maṣdariyya, and the position of the clause is a badal (substitute) from the position of «كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا»; the implied form is: "Have they not seen that they [will not return] to them" (أَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ).
It is also read with a kasra on the hamza, as a resumptive (istiʾnāf) clause.

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ كُلٌّ): it has been dealt with at the end of Hūd.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ الْأَرْضُ الْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَاهَا وَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا فَمِنْهُ يَأْكُلُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ): [«آيَةٌ»] is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَهُمْ» the khabar (predicate). And «الْأَرْضُ» is a mubtadaʾ, and «أَحْيَيْنَاهَا» its khabar; the clause is an explanation of the sign.
It has been said: «الْأَرْضُ» is a mubtadaʾ, «آيَةٌ» is a fronted khabar, «أَحْيَيْنَاهَا» is the explanation of the sign, and «لَهُمْ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «آيَةٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:34-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْعُيُونِ (٣٤) لِيَأْكُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْعُيُونِ): مِنْ, according to the view of al-Akhfash, is redundant (zāʾida); according to the view of others, the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, i.e. "[We caused to gush forth] from the springs what they benefit from" (مِنَ الْعُيُونِ مَا يَنْتَفِعُونَ بِهِ).
(وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ): there are three views on «مَا». The first: it has the meaning of الَّذِي. The second: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa). On both these views it is in the position of a genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ثَمَرَةٍ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «ثَمَرِهِ»]; and it may be accusative, [conjoined] to the position of (مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ).
The third: it is negating.
It is also read without the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. وَمَا عَمِلَتْ]; the three views are possible, except that [taking it as] negating is weak, because «عَمِلَتْ» has no object mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:39-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّى عَادَ كَالْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ (٣٩) لَا الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي لَهَا أَنْ تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ وَلَا اللَّيْلُ سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ وَكُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْقَمَرُ): in the nominative, it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «قَدَّرْنَاهُ» is the khabar (predicate).
And in the accusative, by an implied verb, i.e. "and We measured out the moon" (وَقَدَّرْنَا الْقَمَرَ), because it is conjoined to a noun on which a verb has operated, so it was construed accordingly.
Whoever reads the nominative says: it is construed on (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ) in the two places, and on (الشَّمْسُ), and these are nouns on which no verb has operated.
And (مَنَازِلَ), i.e. "possessing stations" (ذَا مَنَازِلَ); so it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a second mafʿūl (object), because قَدَّرْنَا has the meaning of "We made [it] become" (صَيَّرْنَا). It has been said: the implied form is: "We measured out stations for it" (قَدَّرْنَا لَهُ مَنَازِلَ).
And (الْعُرْجُونُ) is on the pattern فُعْلُول, and the nūn is a root letter.
It has been said: it is augmentative, because it is from الِانْعِرَاج (bending); this is sound in meaning, but irregular in usage.
Some read (سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ) with the accusative [Translator's note: i.e. سَابِقُ النَّهَارَ]; this is weak, and its permissibility rests on the tanwīn having been dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns.
And «يُسَبِّحُونَ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «يَسْبَحُونَ»] is construed as referring to rational beings because they are described with running, swimming, overtaking and outstripping.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَآيَةٌ لَهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّا): it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is that We…" (هِيَ أَنَّا).
It has been said: it is a mubtadaʾ, and «آيَةٌ لَهُمْ» is the khabar; this is permissible because «أَنَّا» is connected with what precedes it.
The hāʾ and the mīm in (ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ) refer to the people of Nūḥ; and it has been said: to the people of Mecca.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلَا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْقَذُونَ (٤٣)).
(فَلَا صَرِيخَ): the majority read it with a fatḥa, and what follows it is then resumptive.
It has been read with the nominative and tanwīn; its explanation is what we mentioned at His saying: (فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَمَتَاعًا إِلَى حِينٍ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا رَحْمَةً): it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun).
It has been said: the implied form is "except by a mercy" (إِلَّا بِرَحْمَةٍ). And it has been said: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ (٤٩)).
(يَخِصِّمُونَ): like His saying (يَهْدِي) [Translator's note: i.e. يَهِدِّي in Yūnus 35], and it has been dealt with in Yūnus.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا يَا وَيْلَنَا مَنْ بَعَثَنَا مِنْ مَرْقَدِنَا هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَصَدَقَ الْمُرْسَلُونَ (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَاوَيْلَنَا): it is like His saying: (يَاحَسْرَةً).
The Kufans said: «وَيْ» is a word, and «لَنَا» is a preposition and its genitive noun.
The majority take «مَنْ بَعَثَنَا» as an interrogative. It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading: مِنْ بَعْثِنَا [Translator's note: the source prints «مَنْ بَعَثَنَا»; the reading meant is with the preposition مِنْ and the maṣdar], taken as a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to وَيْل.
And (هَذَا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مَا وَعَدَ» is the khabar (predicate); «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي, or is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, or is maṣdariyya.
It has been said: هَذَا is a naʿt (adjective) of مَرْقَدِنَا, so one pauses on it; and «مَا وَعَدَ» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "is true" (حَقٌّ) or the like; or it is a khabar whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "this is" (هَذَا), or "[what] raised us is" (بَعَثَنَا).

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ الْيَوْمَ فِي شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي شُغُلٍ): it is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, and «فَاكِهُونَ» is a second khabar; or it [Translator's note: i.e. «فَاكِهُونَ»] is the khabar, and «فِي شُغُلٍ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
It is also read (فَاكِهِينَ), as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase.
And الشُّغُل — with two ḍammas, with a ḍamma followed by a sukūn, with two fatḥas, and with a fatḥa followed by a sukūn — these are dialectal forms, and it has been read with all of them.

ukberi-tibyan:56-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ فِي ظِلَالٍ عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ (٥٦) لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَلَهُمْ مَا يَدَّعُونَ (٥٧) سَلَامٌ قَوْلًا مِنْ رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي ظِلَالٍ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of «هُمْ».
And (عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ) is then resumptive. Or the khabar may be «مُتَّكِئُونَ», with «فِي ظِلَالٍ» a ḥāl (circumstantial) and «عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ» in the accusative by مُتَّكِئُونَ.
And ظِلَال is the plural of ظِلّ, like ذِئْب and ذِئَاب; or of ظُلَّة, like قُبَّة and قِبَاب. And الظُّلَل is the plural of ظُلَّة and nothing else.
(مَا يَدَّعُونَ): there are three views on «مَا»:
It has the meaning of الَّذِي; or it is an indefinite noun; or it is maṣdariyya. Its position is that of a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar is «لَهُمْ». It has been said: the khabar is «سَلَامٌ». It has been said: «سَلَامٌ» is a second adjective (ṣifa) of «مَا». It has been said: «سَلَامٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is peace" (هُوَ سَلَامٌ). And it has been said: it is a badal (substitute) from «مَا».
It is also read in the accusative, as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the omitted hāʾ, i.e. "possessing safety" (ذَا سَلَامَةٍ) or "safe and sound" (مُسْلِمًا).
And (قَوْلًا) is a maṣdar, i.e. "Allah says that to them as a saying" (يَقُولُ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا), or "they say [it] as a saying" (يَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا).
And (مِنْ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of قَوْل.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنْكُمْ جِبِلًّا كَثِيرًا أَفَلَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْقِلُونَ (٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جِبِلًّا): there are many readings of it; all of them are dialectal forms with one meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:69-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ الشِّعْرَ وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ وَقُرْآنٌ مُبِينٌ (٦٩) لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ هُوَ): the pronoun refers to what was taught, i.e. "what He taught him is nothing but a reminder"; «وَمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ» indicates it. (لِتُنْذِرَ): with tāʾ, as address [to the Prophet], and with yāʾ as third person [referring to him], or on the view that it refers to the Qurʾān.

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَذَلَّلْنَاهَا لَهُمْ فَمِنْهَا رَكُوبُهُمْ وَمِنْهَا يَأْكُلُونَ (٧٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَكُوبُهُمْ): with a fatḥa on the rāʾ, i.e. "what they ride" (مَرْكُوبُهُمْ), just as they say حَلُوب with the meaning of مَحْلُوب (milked).
It has been said: it expresses relation (nasab), i.e. "possessing riding" (ذُو رَكُوبٍ).
It has been read «رَكُوبَتُهُمْ», with tāʾ, like حَلُوبَتُهُمْ. And it is read with a ḍamma on the rāʾ, i.e. "that which possesses their riding" (ذُو رَكُوبِهِمْ) [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; presumably ذُو رُكُوبِهِمْ is meant]; or the maṣdar (verbal noun) has the meaning of the passive participle, like الْخَلْق (creation, i.e. what is created).

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلًا وَنَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قَالَ مَنْ يُحْيِي الْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ): with the meaning of رَامّ (decaying) [Translator's note: the source prints «رَامِمٍ»], or of مَرْمُوم (decayed).

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُ إِذَا أَرَادَ شَيْئًا أَنْ يَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ (٨٢)).
(كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): it has been dealt with in Sūrat al-Naḥl. And Allah knows best.
